question:
Run every test method of class `EnvironBuilderFlowTest` in `werkzeug_qa/test_get_environ_m4_dataflow/files/testcase.py` (pytest ids `werkzeug_qa/test_get_environ_m4_dataflow/files/testcase.py::EnvironBuilderFlowTest::test_*`, all methods of the class). During that run, the method `werkzeug.test.EnvironBuilder.get_environ` defined in `src/werkzeug/test.py` (its `def` line is line 677) is invoked a number of times, directly or indirectly (e.g. via `Client.open` -> `EnvironBuilder.get_request`, via `create_environ`, and again for every followed redirect). An invocation is one call of that method; invocations are independent (reaching definitions start fresh at each call). Compute all dynamically observed def-use pairs inside the frame of `get_environ` itself, summed over ALL invocations in ALL test methods of the class.

Tracked variables (exactly these local names of `get_environ`): `_path_encode`, `boundary`, `combined_headers`, `content_length`, `content_type`, `end_pos`, `form_encoded`, `headers`, `input_stream`, `key`, `mimetype`, `raw_uri`, `result`, `self`, `start_pos`, `value`, `values`. Nothing else is tracked: attributes (`self.form`), subscripts (`result[key]`), globals, builtins, and anything inside the body of the nested function `_path_encode` (it runs in its own frame) are ignored.

Definitions (defs): (a) the parameter `self` is defined at the `def` line of `get_environ` at the start of every invocation; (b) a name bound by an assignment statement (plain, annotated, or tuple-unpacking target) is defined at the line where that statement begins; (c) the `def _path_encode(...)` statement defines `_path_encode` at its `def` line; (d) the target names of a `for` statement are defined at the `for` line, once per loop iteration (an iteration = one execution of the loop body). Mutating an object (e.g. `result.update(...)`, `result[k] = v`, `combined_headers[...].append(...)`, `headers.remove(...)`) is NOT a def of the name; it is only a use of it. There are no augmented assignments or comprehensions in this method.

Uses: a tracked name read (loaded) in an executed statement. The use line is the line where the statement begins (for multi-line statements, the first line of the statement, even if the name physically appears on a later line). For an `if`/`elif` the statement is just its condition, used at the `if`/`elif` line each time that condition is evaluated. For a `for` loop, names in the iterable expression are used once each time the loop is entered (not once per iteration), at the `for` line. For an assignment the right-hand side is read before the targets are bound. Within one execution of a statement, a variable that is read several times counts as ONE use (e.g. `self` read five times in one statement execution = one observation). A use inside a loop body counts once per iteration.

A def-use pair (variable, def_line, use_line) is observed each time a use of the variable at use_line is reached by the most recent def of that variable at def_line within the same invocation (dynamic reaching definition along the path actually executed). `count` = the total number of such observations across all invocations in all test methods.

Answer format: a JSON object with a single key `observed_def_use_pairs` whose value is a list of objects with keys `variable` (str, bare local name such as `foo`), `def_line` (int), `use_line` (int), `count` (int >= 1). Line numbers are absolute, 1-based line numbers in `src/werkzeug/test.py` as it exists in the repository. Include only pairs observed at least once; each (variable, def_line, use_line) triple appears exactly once (the count carries the multiplicity). Sort the list ascending by `variable` (Python default `str` ordering, i.e. by code point, so a leading `_` sorts before lowercase letters), then `def_line`, then `use_line` (both numerically).
